steps.title: Declare rotation and window
notes: Every hatch group gets a child group Rotation with start angle and angle increment, and inside it the optional group Limitation window, off by default (OPT_OFF).

The defaults: +67° per layer, and a window 120° wide around the window direction 0° relative to the gas flow. Like the start angle, the window direction is a hatch angle value, so 0° means lines across the flow.

lines: // MPBF background: 67 degrees has no common divisor with 180, so the
// hatch direction repeats only after 180 layers. Default window
// (off by default): hatch LINES perpendicular to the gas flow (gas flow
// angle + 90 degrees), 120 degrees wide -> the lines are never closer
// than 30 degrees to the gas flow direction (see pattern_rotation.js).
// limit_center_angle 0 relative to the gas flow = hatch lines perpendicular
// to the gas flow (hatch angle value convention, see pattern_rotation.js).
exports.create_rotation_group = function(a_parent_grp, a_group_id, a_text, a_defaults, a_flags)
let l_grp = create_child(a_parent_grp, a_group_id, a_text, choose_flags(a_flags, exports.FLAGS.DEF));
// The window is a nested optional group (check box), off by default.
let l_limit = create_child(l_grp, exports.CHILD_ID.ROTATION_LIMIT, a_text, exports.FLAGS.OPT_OFF);

steps.title: Read the settings and the gas flow
notes: read_rotation returns the angles and a limit object. The window direction is relative to the gas flow ('gas_flow') or absolute, measured from +X.
The gas flow angle is a platform parameter: it comes from the platform profile, not from the part's profile.
read_hatch adds against_gas_flow to the rotation: it is the hatch group's Optimized sorting switch, on by default.

steps.title: One angle per layer
notes: Before the hatch of an area is created, get_line_angle computes the angle of this layer from the layer index and the gas flow angle. The pattern functions get it as line_angle.

lines: // Hatch angle of this layer: start angle + layer index * increment
// (default 67 degrees), optionally kept inside a window, e.g. "never
// MPBF background: rotating the lines from layer to layer avoids that
// hatch lines lie exactly on top of each other. The material gets more
// uniform and the residual stress (which is highest along the scan
// direction) is spread over all directions. 67 degrees is a common
// choice because the same angle repeats only after many layers.

steps.title: Rotation without a window
notes: The raw angle is start angle + layer index × increment. 67 has no common divisor with 180, so the line direction repeats only after 180 layers: 133°, 20°, 87°, 154° in layers 50 to 53 of the video.
The value is an angle value for the host's hatch function, where 0 means lines parallel to Y. The line direction on screen is the value + 90°.

lines: // Tip: [a_extra_angle] in the JSDoc means "optional". If the
// caller leaves it out, its value is undefined, so 0 is used instead.
// A window that is off, has no valid width or is 180 degrees or wider
// does not limit anything: plain rotation plus extra angle.

steps.title: Squeeze 180° into the window
notes: With the window on, the whole 180° cycle of directions is compressed linearly onto the window width (map_into_window). Different directions stay different: with a 30° window, layers 50 to 53 get 97.2°, 78.3°, 89.5° and 100.7°, exactly what the video measures.
Relative to the gas flow the window center is gas angle + 180° + window direction: the +180° gives the same lines in reverse order, so they are exposed against the flow.
The code deliberately does not fold the angle back at the window edges: such a fold would map some increments onto a single direction, and every layer would be hatched the same way.

lines: // Distance of the raw angle (plus the sub-group angle) from the
// window center, mapped into the window.
let l_d_map = map_into_window(l_raw + l_extra - l_center, l_limit.width);

steps.title: Turn the order against the gas flow
notes: An angle value gives the lines and their order: the host exposes them one after another along (cos a, sin a). If that direction points downstream, against_gas_flow adds 180°: exactly the same lines, exposed in the opposite order.
That is why the video measures the same line directions as before, but every layer now moves from +X to −X. A direction exactly across the flow is kept.

steps.title: Chess fields and hexagons stay inside, too
notes: Chess and hexagon patterns hatch some cells with an extra +90°, +60° or +120°. angle_with_extra passes that extra angle into the same function, so it is scaled to the window: two chess groups then differ by width / 2 and stay inside the window.

recipes.title: Window on by default
recipes.why: Keep the hatch lines away from the gas flow direction in every new profile.
recipes.result: The limitation window starts switched on with its defaults: lines within 30° … 150° for a gas flow along X.

edits.after: let l_limit = create_child(l_grp, exports.CHILD_ID.ROTATION_LIMIT, a_text, exports.FLAGS.OPT_ON);

recipes.title: A narrower default window
recipes.why: As in the video: hatch lines always nearly perpendicular to the gas flow.
recipes.result: Lines stay within ±30° of the perpendicular once the window is switched on.

recipes.title: Another rotation increment
recipes.why: Some machines and materials use other increments, for example 90° (cross hatching) or 79°.
recipes.result: 79 has no common divisor with 180 either, so the directions repeat after 180 layers. Try 90 in the explainer: only two directions are left, with or without a window.
